title: Ghost-charge detection and idempotent session metering for intermittent streaming clients
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Intermittent websocket/HTTP-streaming client reconnects and replay behavior can generate duplicate or orphaned token attributions, resulting in 'ghost' charges on customer invoices. This ticket implements detection, prevention, and telemetry to ensure idempotent finalization of streaming sessions and to provide a clear reconciliation path for past discrepancies.

Scope: server-side streaming metering pipeline: session lifecycle, checkpointing protocol (session IDs + checkpoint vector), finalization/terminal accounting, and reconciliation/backfill for historical orphaned sessions. Does NOT include embedding/async-batch meter changes (separate work).
root_cause_analysis:
Observed failures: (1) clients reconnect with no session identifier or with a new session ID causing duplicated billing for tokens already consumed; (2) server aggressively finalizes partial fragments on connection tear-down before confirming delivery guarantees; (3) intermediate retries cause mixed attribution between original and retry session IDs because KV checkpoint metadata was lost on transient workers. A sampling of invoices showed >0.7% of streaming sessions in 2026-02 had duplicated output credits.

Contributing factors: client libraries that don't persist server session token, ephemeral worker restarts clearing in-memory checkpoints, and meter-finalization happening based on connection-close events alone without durable checkpoint consensus.
proposed_design:
1) Session identifier contract: require client-sent session_guid (UUID v4) persisted by gateway; if absent, server issues and returns to client. 2) Durable checkpointing: record per-session highest-finalized-offset (HFO) in metering store (append-only journal + compacted view) before acknowledging terminal credits. 3) Two-phase finalization: PROVISIONAL->COMMITTED. Provisionally mark credits at fragment arrival; final COMMITTED state occurs after durable HFO write. 4) Dedup keys: use composite dedup key = sha256(session_guid + model + request_signature + truncated_prefix_hash) to collapse replayed fragments. 5) Reconcile job: nightly backfill to detect orphaned PROVISIONAL records older than retention window and surface candidates for customer adjustments. 6) Metrics & logging: new counters for deduped_fragments, provisional_to_commit_latency, orphaned_provisionals, and ghost_charge_alerts.

Compatibility: design keeps streaming API binary-compatible; clients optionally adopt session_guid to reduce roundtrips. Server issues session_guid when missing.
implementation_plan:
Phase A (Investigation proof-of-concept, 2 wks): instrument tracer to correlate websocket frames to session_guid; prototype HFO writes to metering-store index; add dedupe logic in streaming entrypoint.

Phase B (Core commit, 3 wks): implement two-phase finalization, durable HFO writes, and dedup keys enforcement. Add migration hook to mark existing sessions as legacy for backfill. Update gateway to persist/echo session_guid.

Phase C (Reconcile & backfill, 1 wk): nightly reconcile job and small tool for support to generate customer-facing reconciliation reports.

Phase D (Rollout & monitor, 1 wk): gradual rollout by region with feature flag, enable metrics/alerts.

Owners: Diego (implementation), Priya Nair (metering-store changes), Linh Tran (gateway changes), SRE on-call (deploy coordination).
acceptance_criteria:
- No duplicate final COMMITTED credits for replays with identical dedup-key over 100k synthetic replay tests.
- Provisioned credits must not be considered billable until COMMITTED state persisted to metering-store.
- Deduped_fragments metric incremented when replay occurs; show reduction in ghost_charge_alerts vs baseline after rollout.
- Nightly reconcile job identifies >95% of orphaned provisional records and surfaces them in support report.
- Documentation updated: streaming metering semantics and client session_guid contract.
- Integration tests: deterministic simulation covering worker restart, reconnect-without-guid, and overlapping retries all pass in CI.
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards: Streaming Metering — Dedup & Finalization (per-region). Alerts: ghost_charge_alerts > 5/day for >1 hour (P0), provisional_to_commit_latency p95 > 10s (P1), orphaned_provisionals > 1000/night (P1). Add trace sample for any committed credit lacking HFO write within 30s. Logs: structured events meter.finalize.{provisional|committed|orphan_detected} with dedup_key and session_guid.
test_plan: Unit tests for dedupe-key generation and two-phase finalizer. Integration test harness simulating: client reconnects with same session_guid, reconnects without session_guid, worker restart mid-fragment, and duplicate fragment deliveries. Load test: 100k concurrent streaming sessions with synthetic reconnects; assert no duplicated COMMITTED credits. E2E billing smoke: run billing pipeline against test metering-store and validate final invoice delta < 0.001 baseline after dedupe enabled.
backfill_strategy: Backfill has two parts: (1) Soft reconciliation: nightly job identifies PROVISIONAL records older than 48h and attempts to obtain finalization evidence (HFO or delivery confirmations). If none, mark as candidate for support review. (2) Hard compensation: manual support tool to generate credit adjustments for verified ghost charges. Backfill will tag reconciled records with backfill_run_id and reason. Provide audit CSVs for customers.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: additional durable writes may increase tail latency of streaming finalization. Mitigation: use a lightweight append-only metering-journal with async fsync and commit ack decoupling; allow provisional acknowledged path for low-latency, but only COMMITTED counts to billing (clients can opt-in for lower-latency with provisional display).

Risk: clients that never upgrade will still be able to generate duplicates if they don't persist session_guid. Mitigation: server issues session_guid and returns it; gateway persists mapping to reduce duplicates. Also run client-library rollout and documentation.

Risk: backfill may misclassify legitimate partial sessions as orphaned. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, human review for high-value accounts, and communicate to billing/support teams before automated adjustments.
